import sys, random, pathlib, multiprocessing as mp
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
from chats import ChatStore
root = sys.argv[2]
def worker(n):
    s = ChatStore(root); random.seed(n)
    for i in range(60):
        r = random.random()
        cur = s.list()
        pick = random.choice(cur)["id"] if cur else None
        if r < 0.5:
            s.record(chat_id=pick if random.random() < 0.6 else None, agent_id=str(n % 3),
                     agent_label="a", backend="claude", session_id="x", project_dir="",
                     exchange={"transcript": "hi %d" % i})
        elif r < 0.65 and pick: s.rename(pick, "t%d" % i)
        elif r < 0.8 and pick: s.pin(pick, random.random() < 0.5)
        elif r < 0.9 and pick: s.delete(pick)
        else:
            s.prune("last100"); s.set_current(str(n % 3), pick)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    with mp.Pool(8) as p: p.map(worker, range(8))
    ids = [c["id"] for c in ChatStore(root).list()]
    files = set(p.stem for p in pathlib.Path(root).glob("*.json") if p.name != "index.json")
    print("entries", len(ids), "unique", len(set(ids)), "files", len(files), "match", set(ids) == files)
EOF
python3 -I /tmp/chatstress/stress.py <repo>/daemon /tmp/chatstress/chats; rm -rf /tmp/chatstress

content.text:
No, the list can't show the same chat twice, so I didn't change anything. The QML builds the list only from index.json, and the daemon and the CLI only write that file through one store. That store holds a file lock and drops a chat by id before adding it back. I also ran eight processes at once doing saves, renames, pins, deletes and prunes, and the result was 39 entries, all different, matching the 39 chat files on disk.

The one thing that could look like a duplicate is on purpose. When saving is on, the live conversation shows as "This session" at the top and also as a saved chat marked "in use". The stress script is still in a scratch folder at slash tmp slash chatstress if you want to delete it.
